To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytotoxicity of antitumor drugs is phase specific.

1) the sensitivity to antitumor drugs of DON cells in the S, G 2 -M, or G 1 phase was dependent on the drug, 2) the sensitivity of cells in the G1 -S border was also dependent on the drug and, 3) the sensitivity of DON cells in mitosis was dependent on the type of drug used.

the cell cycle phase specificities of the antitumor drugs tested were as follows: (1) DNA synthesis inhibitors were most cytotoxic in the S phase of the cell; (2) protein synthesis inhibitors were most effective in the S phase; (3) RNA synthesis inhibitors were most toxic in the G 2 phase; (4) the alkylating agent, streptozotocine, was not specific; (5) 5-fluoro-uracil was not specific
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new antitumor drugs, with the study of the mechanism of action of these agents, and with their clinical evaluation.
the cell cycle specificity of antitumors.
the study of the effects of antitumor compounds on the cell cycle of DON cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no single antitumor agent was cytotoxic to cells at a specific phase in the cell cycle.
no single drug was specific for a given cell cycle phase.
agents which inhibit DNA synthesis are most cytotoxic to S-phase cells, whereas agents that inhibit protein and RNA synthesis are most cytogenic to G 1 -phase cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
agents which interfere with DNA synthesis are most toxic to S-phase cells.
agents that were cytotoxic to DON cells at a specific phase are those that inhibit a particular biochemical pathway.

agents that inhibit DNA synthesis were most cytotoxic in the S phase; agents that inhibit protein synthesis were most cytogenic in the S phase, but were also active in the G 2 phase; agents that interfere with RNA synthesis were most cytogenetic at the G 1 /S border region, and agents that inhibit the synthesis of all three major macromolecules were active in all phases of the cell cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytotoxic effects of many agents are phase specific, and that agents that are cytotoxic to cells at specific phases may be useful in the treatment of cancer.
there is no single drug that is cytotoxic only to cells in a particular phase of the cell-cycle.
there are no drugs that are specific for cells in the M phase.
